tomball.drive: This is home base — 22955 TX-249 Ste 26
tomball.housing: Ranch homes and 1990s–2010s subdivisions on architectural shingles, with a growing number of standing-seam and stone-coated steel upgrades along 249.
tomball.storm: Tomball sits in a hail and straight-line wind corridor along SH-249. Spring storms regularly bruise shingles and lift ridge caps in Lakewood and Wildwood.
tomball.note: Core Four Roofing is headquartered in Tomball. When a local homeowner or property manager calls, the crew is already on this side of Harris County — not coming from downtown.

the-woodlands.housing: HOA villages with a heavy mix of concrete tile, architectural shingle, and custom metal. Tile repairs and underlayment failures are common on 1990s–2000s homes.
the-woodlands.storm: Pine-canopy shade keeps decks damp. After a hail week, tile cracks and granule loss show up first on south and west slopes in Sterling Ridge and Creekside Park.
the-woodlands.note: The Woodlands is one of the strongest tile and custom-metal markets we run. HOA architectural rules matter here — we photograph, match the existing profile, and work with the association when a full replace is on the table.

cypress.housing: Master-planned homes from the 2000s forward — lots of architectural shingle, plus tile and stone-coated steel in Bridgeland and Towne Lake.
cypress.storm: Cypress takes Gulf moisture and northwest Harris hail. Low-slope backyard sections and valley leaks show up after the first hard rain of the season.
cypress.note: Cypress homeowners usually want the roof done around school and commute hours. We inspect in Bridgeland and Coles Crossing the same week, then schedule tear-off so the house is dried-in before the next front.

spring.housing: Klein ISD neighborhoods on 20–30 year shingle roofs, with custom homes in Northgate Forest and Gleannloch on tile or metal.
spring.storm: Spring sits under the I-45 hail track. Insurance claims after a Klein or Springwoods storm are a weekly conversation from March through June.
spring.note: Spring is a straight shot down 2920 and I-45 from Tomball. We already run crews through Klein every week, so a leak call in 77379 does not wait on a downtown dispatch.

katy.county: Fort Bend, Harris, and Waller Counties
katy.housing: One of Texas’s densest concrete- and clay-tile belts. Cinco Ranch and Cross Creek Ranch roofs from the late 90s and 2000s are now in the repair-or-replace window.
katy.storm: West-side hail and tropical remnants stall over Katy. Broken tiles, failed underlayment, and valley rust are the usual call — not a full shingle tear-off.
katy.note: Katy is a tile town. We repair clay and concrete tile, and when the deck or underlayment is gone we talk stone-coated steel: same look, less weight, better in hail. Cinco Ranch and Cross Creek Ranch are weekly stops.

fulshear.housing: Newer master-planned and custom homes — tile, standing seam, and stone-coated steel on larger footprints than a typical Houston tract house.
fulshear.storm: Open prairie west of Katy means higher wind. Ridge and hip tiles walk first. Custom metal needs seam and flashing checks after a derecho.
fulshear.note: Fulshear jobs are larger and more architectural. We price tile repair, full tile replace, and stone-coated steel as three honest options.

sugar-land.housing: Established Fort Bend neighborhoods with a lot of concrete tile and aged architectural shingle. Telfair and First Colony still show original 90s tile.
sugar-land.storm: Sugar Land takes the same hail as southwest Houston, plus humidity that cooks underlayment under tile. We find wet decks that still look fine from the street.
sugar-land.note: Sugar Land homeowners often want the tile look kept. We repair where the system is sound and convert to stone-coated steel when the underlayment or deck has given up.

conroe.housing: A mix of older in-town roofs, new construction around Grand Central Park, and lake homes that see more wind-driven rain.
conroe.storm: Lake Conroe winds drive rain under ridge and chimney flashings. Metal and tile on the water need different detailing than a tract house in 77304.
conroe.note: Conroe is a Montgomery County run we already make for The Woodlands. Lake homes and new-construction punch lists are common — we do not treat them like a Houston starter house.

humble.housing: Established east-side neighborhoods on 15–25 year shingles, plus newer Fall Creek homes and commercial along 59.
humble.storm: Humble sits on the US-59 storm path. After a spring cell, we see bruised shingles and lifted flashing on the same blocks as last year’s claims.
humble.note: We inspect along 1960 and 59, and we keep Atascocita and Fall Creek on the same east-side route as Humble.

atascocita.housing: 2000s master-planned homes — architectural shingle with some tile and metal on larger Eagle Springs and Walden lots.
atascocita.storm: East Harris storms stack up against the lake breeze. We see repeat leak calls at chimneys and skylights after a wet week in 77346.
atascocita.note: Atascocita is not a Humble add-on. Homeowners in Eagle Springs want a crew that already knows the HOA and the typical 20-year shingle failure.

houston.drive: Northwest Houston is 15–30 minutes from Tomball HQ
houston.housing: We focus on northwest Houston — Champions, Willowbrook, Copperfield — not a downtown-only promise. Shingle, tile, and metal all show up inside the Beltway and along 249.
houston.storm: NW Houston takes the same hail as Tomball and Cypress. After a Willowbrook or Champions storm, insurance documentation and a fast dry-in matter more than a cheap square price.
houston.note: From Tomball we cover northwest Houston the same day — Champions, Willowbrook, Copperfield, and the 249 corridor. That is the Houston we can actually reach, not a downtown-only promise.

pasadena.housing: Older residential stock plus a large industrial and commercial footprint along the Ship Channel side.
pasadena.storm: Pasadena sees Gulf humidity, industrial fallout, and tropical rain. Fasteners and flashings corrode faster than they do in The Woodlands.
pasadena.note: Pasadena work is often a mix of home repairs and commercial roofs near the Channel. We schedule east-side days so a residential leak and a nearby commercial survey can share a trip.

pearland.housing: 2000s–2010s master-planned homes, mostly architectural shingle, with tile and metal in Shadow Creek Ranch and custom pockets.
pearland.storm: South-side storms come off the Gulf. We see wind-lifted edges and soaked insulation after a slow-moving tropical rain more than classic hail bruises.
pearland.note: Pearland is a south-ring city we add when the schedule is tight and the job is a real leak or replace — not a fishing trip. Shadow Creek and Silverlake inspections get a dedicated south-side day.

league-city.housing: Coastal-adjacent homes with wind ratings that matter. Tile, dimensional shingle, and some metal on the water and in Tuscan Lakes.
league-city.storm: League City is a wind city. Code and fastening matter more here than in Tomball. After a tropical system we check ridges, eaves, and garage-door-adjacent flashing first.
league-city.note: League City roofs take Gulf wind. Residential calls get a wind-aware spec — we do not copy a north-Houston shingle detail onto a 77573 house.

missouri-city.housing: Sienna and Quail Valley carry a lot of tile and HOA-controlled shingle. Lots are larger; scaffolding and dumpster plans matter.
missouri-city.storm: Fort Bend storms stall over Sienna the same way they do over Sugar Land. Tile underlayment and valley metal are the usual failure points.
missouri-city.note: Missouri City is a Fort Bend tile-and-HOA market. We work Sienna specs.

baytown.housing: Working-class and industrial-adjacent housing plus commercial along 146 and I-10. Metal and shingle dominate; some tile on newer tracts.
baytown.storm: Baytown gets Gulf air and industrial moisture. Fasteners rust. We spec coastal-aware fasteners on metal and do not reuse tired pipe jacks.
baytown.note: Baytown days are often mixed residential repair and commercial survey. We batch east Harris so a 77521 home leak and a nearby plant-adjacent roof can be seen the same trip.

richmond.housing: Fast-growing west Fort Bend — new construction plus 15–20 year roofs in Pecan Grove and Aliana. Tile shows up on the larger plans.
richmond.storm: Open land west of 99 means wind. New-construction punch-list leaks and aged Pecan Grove shingles both show up after the same front.
richmond.note: Richmond and Rosenberg share a west-side day. We inspect Aliana and Pecan Grove with the same crew that runs Katy tile that week.

rosenberg.housing: Older in-town roofs plus new tracts toward Richmond. A practical mix of shingle repair and the occasional metal barn-adjacent shop we will not confuse with a house.
rosenberg.storm: Rosenberg storms come across open Fort Bend fields. We see edge lift and poorly fastened starter courses on newer production homes.
rosenberg.note: Rosenberg is on the Richmond / Fulshear route. If the roof is a house, we treat it like a house — not a metal-building kit job.

friendswood.housing: Mature trees and 1980s–2000s homes. Shingle and some tile. Tree-limb and moss issues are as common as hail.
friendswood.storm: Friendswood’s canopy hides granule loss and soft decking. We walk it after storms and after a quiet wet winter — both create leaks.
friendswood.note: Friendswood homeowners care about the trees and the HOA. We tarp, trim coordination, and match shingle lines so the street view stays clean.

alvin.housing: Smaller-town stock — older shingle, some metal, agricultural edges we keep separate from the house spec.
alvin.storm: Brazoria storms are wet and windy. We see more edge-metal and porch-roof leaks than fancy tile failures.
alvin.note: Alvin is a south-county stop we pair with Pearland or Friendswood. Honest repair first; replace when the deck says so.

dickinson.housing: Coastal humidity and bayou moisture. Shingle and metal. Salt air shortens fastener and jack life.
dickinson.storm: Dickinson takes tropical rain and bayou flood-adjacent humidity. We check underlayment and rusted flashings even when the shingles still look dark from the street.
dickinson.note: Dickinson roofs fail from moisture as much as from hail. We write the spec for Galveston County weather, not a north-Houston default.

galveston.housing: Historic, coastal, and vacation homes. Metal, tile, and specialty systems that have to take salt and wind. This is not a three-tab market.
galveston.storm: Galveston is wind, salt, and hurricane code. Fastening patterns, coastal metals, and historic detailing are the job — not a suburban shingle overlay.
galveston.note: Galveston work is scheduled as its own coastal day. We do metal and tile the island actually needs, and we do not pretend a Tomball shingle crew can freehand a historic East End roof.

austin.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 2.5 hours
austin.housing: Hill Country stone, tile, and standing seam on northwest Austin and lake homes. Cedar and hail both show up on the same roof.
austin.storm: Austin hail is real, and the sun cooks underlayment faster than Houston humidity does. Lake-side metal needs different flashing than a tract house in Round Rock.
austin.note: The office is in Tomball. Austin-area jobs are scheduled Texas coverage. We still write the spec for Steiner Ranch tile or Four Points metal.

round-rock.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 2.5 hours
round-rock.housing: Production and custom homes north of Austin. Architectural shingle with tile and metal in Teravista and Forest Creek.
round-rock.storm: Williamson County hail is frequent in spring. We document like an insurance job even when the homeowner has not opened a claim yet.
round-rock.note: Round Rock is on the Austin-north circuit with Georgetown and Hutto. We batch those inspections so the trip is a real production day.

georgetown.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 2.75 hours
georgetown.housing: Sun City and custom Hill Country homes — tile, metal, and low-slope sections that leak at walls. Older limestone houses need careful flashing.
georgetown.storm: Georgetown hail and sun. Tile on Sun City roofs is a regular repair. We do not walk those tiles like a shingle roof.
georgetown.note: Georgetown work is often HOA or 55+ community sensitive. We keep the site clean and the tile count honest.

cedar-park.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 2.5 hours
cedar-park.housing: 1990s–2010s suburban roofs. Shingle first, with metal and tile on the larger Brushy Creek plans.
cedar-park.storm: Cedar Park takes the same hail as NW Austin. After a cell we see bruised shingles on south slopes and cracked pipe boots.
cedar-park.note: Cedar Park and Leander share a day. We inspect Buttercup Creek and Ranch at Brushy Creek as one northwest Austin loop.

leander.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 2.75 hours
leander.housing: Fast growth — new construction plus hillside custom. Metal and tile on Travisso and Crystal Falls; shingle on the production streets.
leander.storm: Hillside wind and hail. New-construction leaks at walls are as common as storm claims.
leander.note: Leander jobs are often larger and newer. We still check the deck — new does not mean dry.

pflugerville.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 2.5 hours
pflugerville.housing: Production homes from the 2000s. Architectural shingle, some tile. HOA streets want a clean tear-off.
pflugerville.storm: Pflugerville hail is a spring ritual. We photograph like a claim and keep the dumpster off the HOA grass.
pflugerville.note: Pflugerville pairs with Round Rock and Hutto. One north-Austin day, several streets, no wasted trip.

manor.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 2.6 hours
manor.housing: Newer east-Austin growth. Shingle on most plans, metal accents, some tile.
manor.storm: Open fields mean wind. We see starter-course and drip-edge failures on newer Manor roofs after a front.
manor.note: Manor is on the east Travis loop with Pflugerville. We batch those inspections instead of a one-off drive.

kyle.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 2.75 hours
kyle.housing: South of Austin production homes plus new 6 Creeks plans. Shingle and some tile.
kyle.storm: Hays County storms run up I-35. We see the same bruised shingle pattern after a spring week as we do in Buda.
kyle.note: Kyle and Buda are one south-Austin day. We do not send a crew for a single soft-lead and call it coverage.

buda.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 2.7 hours
buda.housing: Small-city and new-suburb mix. Shingle, some metal. Historic downtown needs a lighter touch.
buda.storm: Buda takes I-35 hail. Sunfield and Garlic Creek roofs are now in the first replacement cycle.
buda.note: Buda pairs with Kyle. Historic downtown roofs and new Sunfield roofs get different specs on the same trip.

hutto.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 2.6 hours
hutto.housing: Newer Williamson County tracts. Shingle first. Some metal and tile on larger Star Ranch plans.
hutto.storm: Hutto hail looks like Round Rock hail. We document and replace by the slope, not the whole street, unless the photos say otherwise.
hutto.note: Hutto is on the Round Rock / Pflugerville circuit. Same-day cluster inspections keep the Texas trip honest.

lakeway.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 2.75 hours
lakeway.housing: Hill Country and lake custom — tile, slate-look, standing seam, and complicated valleys. These are not tract-shingle roofs.
lakeway.storm: Lake wind and hail. Custom metal seams and tile hips fail first. Access and steep pitches change the production plan.
lakeway.note: Lakeway jobs are custom. We price tile, metal, and stone-coated steel like a Hill Country roof, not a Houston starter house.

dallas.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 3.5 hours
dallas.housing: North Dallas custom and mid-century — tile, slate, and complicated flashings. We are not bidding every 752 zip; we take the roofs that match the work.
dallas.storm: Dallas hail is legendary. Tile and slate after a Preston Hollow storm need a crew that will not walk the roof to death.
dallas.note: Dallas-area work is scheduled Texas coverage from Tomball. We write a North Dallas spec for tile and slate — we do not spray a Houston shingle price across 75225.

fort-worth.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 3.5 hours
fort-worth.housing: West-side custom and older FW stock. Tile, metal, and some slate. Mira Vista and Tanglewood are not production shingle streets.
fort-worth.storm: Tarrant hail. We document and repair tile without treating it like a 3-tab claim.
fort-worth.note: Fort Worth pairs with Arlington and Grand Prairie when we run a DFW week. Custom west-side roofs get their own production plan.

arlington.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 3.5 hours
arlington.housing: 1970s–2000s suburban roofs. Shingle and tile. A lot of first-generation architectural shingle at end of life.
arlington.storm: Arlington hail is frequent. Insurance documentation is part of the inspection, not an upsell.
arlington.note: Arlington is a DFW week stop with Fort Worth. We batch southwest Arlington streets instead of a one-roof drive from Tomball.

plano.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 3.75 hours
plano.housing: HOA-heavy Collin County. Tile and high-end shingle in West Plano and Willow Bend. Legacy-area commercial sits next to custom homes.
plano.storm: Plano hail. HOAs want matching tile and a clean site. We plan dumpsters and material staging before the tear-off.
plano.note: Plano, Frisco, and Allen are one north-DFW loop. Tile and HOA rules are the job as much as the weather.

frisco.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 3.75 hours
frisco.housing: Newer luxury and production. Tile, stone-coated steel, and standing seam on the larger plans. HOA architectural committees are active.
frisco.storm: Frisco hail on tile is a cracked-hip problem. We count tiles and check underlayment instead of guessing from the driveway.
frisco.note: Frisco pairs with Prosper and McKinney. We show up with a tile and metal plan, not a cheap shingle default.

mckinney.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 3.8 hours
mckinney.housing: Historic squares plus huge new tracts. Tile and shingle. Downtown needs a different crew plan than Trinity Falls.
mckinney.storm: Collin County hail. New-construction wall leaks and aged downtown flashings both show up after the same week.
mckinney.note: McKinney is on the Frisco / Allen loop. Historic and new-construction roofs do not get the same spec.

allen.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 3.75 hours
allen.housing: HOA suburbs with tile and architectural shingle. Twin Creeks is a regular tile conversation.
allen.storm: Allen hail. We match tile and keep the HOA happy on dumpster placement.
allen.note: Allen sits between Plano and McKinney. We inspect Twin Creeks on the same north-Collin day.

lewisville.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 3.6 hours
lewisville.housing: 1980s–2010s Denton County stock. Shingle and some tile. Lake-adjacent humidity on the east side.
lewisville.storm: Lewisville hail and lake moisture. We check jacks and flashings that rusted between storms.
lewisville.note: Lewisville, The Colony, and Flower Mound are one Denton-county day.

the-colony.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 3.7 hours
the-colony.housing: Newer lakefront and mixed-use. Tile, metal, and production shingle in the same zip.
the-colony.storm: Open lake wind. Ridge tiles and standing-seam terminations get the first look after a storm.
the-colony.note: The Colony is on the Frisco / Lewisville loop. Lakefront metal and HOA tile get different details.

flower-mound.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 3.6 hours
flower-mound.housing: Custom and HOA homes — tile, metal, and high-end shingle. Bridlewood is not a starter-house spec.
flower-mound.storm: Denton hail on custom tile. We walk designated paths and count broken pieces instead of a full tear-off default.
flower-mound.note: Flower Mound custom roofs are scheduled with Lewisville. We bring a tile and metal plan, not a three-tab bid.

prosper.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 3.8 hours
prosper.housing: New luxury tracts. Tile and standing seam on large plans. HOAs are picky and the roofs are steep.
prosper.storm: North Collin hail on brand-new tile. We still check underlayment — new is not the same as right.
prosper.note: Prosper pairs with Frisco. Windsong and Gentle Creek jobs are production-planned, not a two-man punch list.

irving.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 3.5 hours
irving.housing: Las Colinas commercial plus Valley Ranch and Hackberry Creek homes. Mixed tile, metal, and TPO next door to each other.
irving.storm: Irving hail hits both office parks and HOA streets. We keep commercial TPO and residential tile on separate work orders.
irving.note: Irving is a DFW week city. Las Colinas commercial and Valley Ranch residential can share a trip — not a spec.

garland.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 3.6 hours
garland.housing: Older Dallas-county stock plus Firewheel. Shingle and some tile. A lot of first replacements.
garland.storm: Garland hail. We see 20-year shingles that have been through more than one claim cycle.
garland.note: Garland is on the east-DFW loop. Honest repair vs replace — we do not re-shingle a wet deck to close a claim.

grand-prairie.drive: Texas coverage from Tomball — about 3.5 hours
grand-prairie.housing: Between Dallas and Fort Worth — production homes, some tile in Lake Ridge, commercial along I-30 and 360.
grand-prairie.storm: Grand Prairie takes both Dallas and Tarrant hail tracks. Lake Ridge tile and west-side shingle fail differently after the same cell.
grand-prairie.note: Grand Prairie sits on the Arlington / Irving day. We split residential tile from commercial surveys so the spec stays clean.

tx.drive: Headquartered in Tomball, covering Houston, Austin, and DFW
tx.housing: Houston-suburb homes are the daily work. Austin and Dallas–Fort Worth jobs are scheduled as Texas coverage, with a spec that matches that metro’s weather and materials.
tx.storm: Texas hail, Gulf wind, and Hill Country sun are different problems. A Galveston metal roof and a Frisco tile roof do not get the same detail.
tx.note: Core Four Roofing is a Tomball company that takes Texas work. Houston-suburb crews run daily. Austin and Dallas–Fort Worth jobs are scheduled.
